title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): S = Spec Q. Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q). Γ_Q^+ is the kernel of the full cyclotomic character, i.e. Gal(Q̄/Q(μ_∞)) = Gal(Q̄/Q^ab). Each prime p ∈ Q^* = G_m(Q) gives a Kummer homomorphism ζ_p : Γ_Q^+ → Ẑ(1), σ ↦ (σ(p^{1/n})/p^{1/n})_n. These maps are honest homomorphisms because Γ_Q^+ fixes all roots of unity. Question (a) asks whether ζ_p is surjective or at least has open image. Question (b) asks whether the ζ_p are Ẑ-linearly independent, i.e. whether (ζ_{p1},…,ζ_{pn}) has open image.

On this page Grothendieck splits ζ_p into its ℓ-components ζ_{p,ℓ} : Γ_Q^+ → Z_ℓ(1). He wants to prove ("au moins!") that each component is surjective, or surjective for all but finitely many ℓ and with open image for every ℓ.
- Each ζ_{p,ℓ} is the Kummer map attached to the ℓ-power isogeny tower 1 → μ_n → G_m → G_m → 1 (λ ↦ λ^n, n = ℓ^ν), evaluated on the tower of inverse images of p.
- To study it he localizes at ℓ. He takes 'the' decomposition group D_ℓ = Gal(Q̄_ℓ/Q_ℓ) ↪ Γ_Q, defined up to conjugacy, hence the quotation marks. On it he considers the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character χ_ℓ : D_ℓ → Z_ℓ^*.
- Better, he restricts to the inertia group I_ℓ ⊂ D_ℓ and sets I_ℓ^+ = Ker(χ_ℓ|I_ℓ).

Key observation: I_ℓ^+ ⊂ Γ_Q^+. The reason is that for ℓ' ≠ ℓ the character χ_{ℓ'} is unramified at ℓ, so trivial on I_ℓ. It is not trivial on D_ℓ, since Frobenius acts on μ_{ℓ'^∞} by ℓ. Concretely, I_ℓ^+ = Gal(Q̄_ℓ / Q_ℓ^{ur}(μ_{ℓ^∞})).

The next page then asks whether the local restriction ζ_{p,ℓ}|I_ℓ^+ is surjective or has open image. This is a strategy of bounding the global image from below by a local, purely ramified piece: local Kummer theory of p over Q_ℓ^{ur}(μ_{ℓ^∞}).
errors: The hoped-for surjectivity of ζ_{p,ℓ} for every ℓ fails at ℓ = 2. Every quadratic field Q(√p) lies in a cyclotomic field: √(±p) via Gauss sums, √2 ∈ Q(μ_8). So √p ∈ Q^ab, Γ_Q^+ fixes √p, and ζ_{p,2}(Γ_Q^+) ⊂ 2Z_2(1).

For ℓ odd, ζ_{p,ℓ} is surjective. Overall the image of ζ_p is 2Z_2 × ∏_{ℓ odd} Z_ℓ: open, index 2. Grothendieck's fallback formulation ('surjective except for finitely many ℓ, open image for all ℓ') is the correct one.
Minor: the embedding D_ℓ → Γ_Q is only defined up to conjugation, which Grothendieck signals with quotes. This is harmless for kernels of characters, since χ is central/abelian.
Equation number (359) appears to be reused: the previous page already has (359) for ζ_{p,ℓ}.

ideas.what: Kummer characters ζ_p : Gal(Q̄/Q(μ_∞)) → Ẑ(1) attached to primes p, and the questions of surjectivity / open image / independence
ideas.modern_name: Kummer theory over Q^ab = Q(μ_∞); image of Galois in the 'false Tate' / Kummer–cyclotomic extensions; Bashmakov–Ribet type openness for G_m
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Kummer theory; Schinzel (abelian binomials, 1977); Bashmakov and Ribet for the general Kummer-theory openness
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA; possibly related to remarks in La Longue Marche, unsure

ideas.what: Localizing at ℓ: decomposition group D_ℓ, ℓ-adic cyclotomic character, inertia I_ℓ, and I_ℓ^+ = ker(χ_ℓ|I_ℓ) ⊂ Γ_Q^+ because χ_{ℓ'} is unramified at ℓ
ideas.modern_name: Local–global argument via inertia; Gal(Q̄_ℓ/Q_ℓ^{ur}(μ_{ℓ^∞})) embedded in Gal(Q̄/Q^ab)

ideas.what: Reading Kummer classes as monodromy of the isogeny tower λ ↦ λ^{ℓ^ν} on G_m, i.e. inverse images of the point p
ideas.modern_name: Arboreal/Kummer tower of a torus; ℓ-adic Kummer representation of a rational point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Kummer; Serre/Ribet for tori and abelian varieties)

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up a standard local argument (inertia at ℓ inside Gal(Q̄/Q^ab)) to study Kummer characters of primes. The answers (open image, index 2 at ℓ = 2 because √p ∈ Q^ab) are classical. The only mildly interesting point is the motivation from a 'Fermat context' with p = 2 on the previous page, but nothing on this page goes beyond known Kummer theory.
transcription_corrections: 'Étudier Σ_{p,e}[?], i.e.' should read 'Étudier ζ_{p,ℓ}, i.e.' (the Kummer component, not Σ).
'et : isog[?] ...[?] pour ∀ l' is very abbreviated. It is probably a phrase like 'et à image ouverte pour ∀ ℓ' (open image for all ℓ). It is not about isogenies; the reading is uncertain.
The equation number before the exact sequence looks like '(339)' in the image but is presumably (359) bis / a reused number.
In (361) the struck-out character before the equation number is a deleted label; read D_ℓ = π_1(Q_ℓ, Q̄_ℓ) ↪ Γ_Q (with Q̄_ℓ as base point).
